Swiss Ski Trip 2027

Beginner-friendly, budget to mid-tier resorts for a January–February trip from New York. Prices are for winter 2026/27 in Swiss francs (CHF ≈ USD) unless noted.

Resort shortlist

#1 Top pickZurich

Arosa Lenzerheide

225 km of groomed slopes up to 2,865 m and the highest share of easy terrain of any Swiss resort (58%). Gentle nursery areas in both villages, Ski School Nova in Lenzerheide.

Beginner pass
CHF 49/day · CHF 221/6 days
Full pass
CHF 89/day · CHF 401/6 days (dynamic; seen at CHF 63 online)
Lodging
~CHF 141/night (Chesa Clois apt, Jan 9–30) vs ~185 in Feb
Getting there
~2.5 hrs from Zurich by train; ski pass includes local bus/train

Downside: not on Magic Pass; many hotels need a ski-bus ride.

Lift tickets →
Geneva pickGeneva

Villars-Gryon-Les Diablerets

104 km of slopes, 66% easy terrain, and a dedicated Beginners' Pass covering nursery lifts in all three villages. Glacier 3000 is the backup if snow is thin.

Beginner pass
CHF 45/day · CHF 90/2 days
Full pass
CHF 75/day; Alpes Vaudoises CHF 379/6 days (save up to 50% online)
Lodging
Stay in Gryon, Ollon or Aigle to save; free local transport with ski pass
Getting there
~2¼ hrs from Geneva; "Easy Ski" deal from CHF 69

Downside: village hotels can get pricey; mostly mid-altitude.

Lift tickets →
Zurich

Engelberg-Titlis

Very snow-sure glacier area with cheap local beginner zones. Easy access from Zurich via Lucerne.

Beginner areas
Gerschnialp CHF 31 · Trübsee CHF 44 · Brunni CHF 48/day
Full pass
~CHF 67–68/day (dynamic); Snow'n'Rail 20% off
Lodging
Hotel Belmont*** ~CHF 180/night w/ breakfast (Jan 4–27)
Getting there
~1¾ hrs from Zurich Airport

Downside: famous Titlis runs are mostly intermediate+; gets busy.

Prices →

Small, family-friendly area with lots of easy blue slopes. Cheapest full-mountain pass on the list and on the Magic Pass.

Hotel Sörenberg doubles CHF 118–190 w/ breakfast
Getting there

Closest serious resort to Zurich, with two practice areas, magic carpets and a cheap beginner-lift pass.

Ways to save

Go mid-JanuaryEvery lodging rate checked is cheaper Jan 4–29 than at Christmas or from Jan 30 into February school holidays, and flights bottom out Jan 14–27.
Start on the beginner ticketIt's roughly half the full-mountain price. Upgrade only once you're ready for bigger runs.
Swiss Half Fare CardCHF 150 for a month of half-price trains and buses. Better than a Swiss Travel Pass (CHF 254–399) for a one-resort ski week.
Snow'n'RailBook train + ski pass together on SBB: 20% off Engelberg passes, up to 30% off Flumserberg.
Stay in the cheaper townLenzerheide or Chur instead of Arosa, Gryon/Aigle instead of Villars, Saas-Grund instead of Saas-Fee.
Skip the Magic PassAt CHF 786 it only pays off past ~9–10 ski days or several resorts.
Book lift tickets earlyDynamic pricing at Arosa Lenzerheide, Engelberg and Villars rewards booking online in advance.
Budget for rentalsAbout CHF 245/week for skis + boots, plus ~CHF 63 for a helmet (Intersport benchmark).
Compiled Nov 2026 from official resort, SBB and Google Flights pages. Prices change; confirm before booking.
